clue.text: Business that produces jam, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: trade or dealing, as in the drug business
second meaning: the vehicles on a road, which can build into a jam

explanation.surface: A factory that makes jam, like a fruit-preserves firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The jam is not fruit but a queue of cars; the word for vehicles on the road also means illicit trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is used for dealing or commerce, especially illegal dealing, and also for road vehicles that cause congestion.

clue.text: I, for one, will often get depressed by such a worker

parts.words: I, for one, will often get depressed by such a worker
parts.note: surface reading: a gloomy employee makes the speaker feel low
setter's reading: the letter I is one key on a keyboard, pressed down repeatedly by someone typing

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that a certain colleague tends to get them down.
explanation.walkthrough: Depressed means pressed down, and I is not the speaker but a letter key.
explanation.definitionFit: A person employed to type documents presses keyboard keys all day, including the key for that letter.

clue.text: It provokes defensive reaction from enemy with intelligence

parts.note: an anti is someone opposed, an opponent
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An army responds defensively when the foe turns up with spy reports.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreign substance that triggers the body's immune system to make antibodies against it.

clue.text: Laugh immoderately as Jack gets into quarrel

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to fall out is to quarrel
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: People laugh wildly when a man called Jack joins in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall about is an idiom for being helpless with laughter, collapsing in mirth.

clue.text: Prominent decoration given by King or Queen?

parts.words: Prominent decoration given by King or Queen
parts.note: surface reading: an honour or medal awarded by the monarch
setter's reading: these are chessmen standing in the middle of the back rank

explanation.surface: A grand medal handed out by the reigning monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: On a chessboard the king and queen start on the two middle squares of the back row.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrepiece is the main ornament on a table, and the chess king and queen are the pieces in the middle.

clue.text: Mistake a call of derision for something really frightful

parts.note: a bug is an error, as in software
taken as written
a boo is a jeer

explanation.surface: Someone takes a jeer to be something truly terrifying.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugaboo is a bogey or bugbear, an object of fear or dread.

clue.text: Community effort for social worker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gathering of neighbours to work together
second meaning: an insect living in a colony, where workers do the labour

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood project set up for someone in social services.
explanation.walkthrough: A social worker here is not a caseworker but an insect from a hive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a communal working party and a colonial insect, whose worker caste does the hive's labour.

clue.text: Assumed fact, putting two and two together in information

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
two and two make four, IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Something taken for granted once the clues are combined into a conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Putting two and two together looks like the idiom for deducing; here it is plain arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A given is a fact accepted as a starting point without needing proof.

clue.text: One of the Brontes — the fashionable one — was an artist

parts.note: the Brontë sisters published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell
in means fashionable
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A claim that the most stylish Brontë sister was secretly a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the name of a Venetian painter family; 'was an artist' stands for a person who was one.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Bellini and his relatives were Renaissance painters of Venice, so the surname names a past artist.

clue.text: Take precedence over, in exit, say?

indicators.note: say means the words are only to be spoken, matched by their sound

parts.note: an exit is a way out, its two words put in the other order

explanation.surface: Something has priority over the matter of leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To outweigh is to be more important or significant than something, so it ranks higher.

clue.text: Favourite clue an anagram? It may appear in crossword, so to speak

definitions.text: It may appear in crossword, so to speak

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: the word itself tells us the following letters are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter's favourite clue is an anagram, a feature found in every crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross word, split in two, is an angry word; 'so to speak' warns of that play.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulky irritability shows itself in cross, ill-tempered remarks, the cross words of the definition.

clue.text: The dance hasn't finished, man

indicators.note: not finished means the word stops short of its end

parts.note: the valeta is an old-time ballroom dance

explanation.surface: Someone tells a man that the dance is still going on.
explanation.definitionFit: Man here means manservant, a gentleman's personal attendant, as in 'my man will see you out'.

clue.text: Heel of Achilles, literally

parts.note: surface reading: the hero's one vulnerable spot
setter's reading: take the heel as the final letter of the name, written in Greek

explanation.surface: A reference to the Greek hero's famous weak point.
explanation.walkthrough: Literally means by letters: the heel is the last letter of the hero's name, and in Greek that letter has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name ends in S, and the Greek alphabet calls that letter by this name, as a final character.

clue.text: Direct one production that's profound

indicators.note: a production is something made, so these letters are made into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to direct a single show of real depth.
explanation.walkthrough: Direct and production suggest the theatre; production is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite describes knowledge that is obscure and deep, understood only by few, so profound fits.

clue.text: Clumsy and old-fashioned in hack work

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters inside the phrase that follows, splitting it open

parts.note: to hack is to chop, so hack work is chopping

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made into something, so the word before it is remodelled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hack writer's output is both clumsy and dated, the critic sniffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-fashioned' reads as one hyphenated adjective, but the hyphen hides a word followed by its anagram signal; 'hack work' suggests poor writing, yet means cutting with an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a heavy-footed, awkward person, and clodhopping describes such lumbering, graceless movement.

clue.text: Obdurate Scot's very likely to embrace maiden

indicators.note: an embrace wraps around, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: unco is Scots for very
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
promising means likely to succeed

explanation.surface: A stubborn Scotsman is quite likely to hug a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Unco is a Scots word for very; the phrase unco promising, very likely, wraps around the maiden.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly refusing to change, unwilling to give way or meet halfway.

clue.text: Transient reforms without delay

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so these letters take a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fleeting changes made without hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Instanter is a legal or jocular word meaning immediately, at once.

clue.text: Person who opposes aim — nothing right with it?

parts.note: an object is a goal
nought, zero
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone opposing a goal asks whether anything is right about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises protests or registers disagreement, such as a conscientious objector.

clue.text: Sound a small instrument to reveal what's wrong

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally play a little pipe
second meaning: expose wrongdoing, as an informer does

explanation.surface: A referee pipes up to signal a foul.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for exposing misconduct comes from a referee stopping play, and literally means piping a small instrument.

clue.text: Displacing son in expedition

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: an outing is a trip
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A son pushes others aside on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousting means driving someone out of a position and taking their place, so it is removing.

clue.text: Bounty — a big ship

parts.note: large means big
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: The Bounty described as a sizeable vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Bounty looks like the famous mutiny ship; here it means generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving of gifts or money, which is what a bounty is.

clue.text: Minute left in which to see a second animal

indicators.note: in which means the first part holds the others inside it

parts.note: wee means tiny
taken as written
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A minute remains in which to spot another creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Minute is the adjective tiny, not sixty seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: A small slender carnivorous mammal that hunts rodents, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Part of London — poor quarter? Just the reverse

parts.note: east is a quarter of the compass
cheap means of poor quality
an instruction to swap the order of the two words, not to read letters backwards

explanation.surface: A cheap district of London, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the reverse' swaps the order of the two words, not their letters. Eastcheap is a street in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastcheap is a historic street in the City of London, once a medieval market, so a part of it.

clue.text: Rising leader associated with martial centre?

definitions.text: Rising leader associated with martial centre?

parts.note: surface reading: an up-and-coming chief
setter's reading: a future officer attached to a military academy

explanation.surface: An ambitious commander linked to some military base.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee officer at a military college is a leader in the making, still rising through training.

clue.text: Assent a European king withheld

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something withheld is kept back, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a Greek is a European
chess abbreviation

explanation.surface: A European king holds back his approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to consent or concur, the same as saying yes to a proposal.

clue.text: Riding for a place

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Yorkshire was divided into three ridings
second meaning: a finishing position in a race, behind first and second

explanation.surface: A jockey rides in hope of getting placed.
explanation.walkthrough: A riding was one of the three administrative divisions of Yorkshire, a historic English county; the word comes from Old Norse for one of three parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Each riding was a one-of-three share of the county, and the bronze position in a race is also called this.

clue.text: Tis more or equally pure

wordplay.note: something that is more or equal is, in colloquial contracted speech, not less than the other

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned boast that something is greater or at least as good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T ain't less is a dialect way of saying it is not less, which is to say more or equal.
explanation.definitionFit: Without any stain or blemish, unspoilt and untainted, so entirely clean.

clue.text: Honour apparent to ingoing PM

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in bridge the ace, king, queen, jack and this card are the honours
second meaning: the number on the door of Downing Street that a new prime minister sees

explanation.surface: An award visible to the incoming prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The British prime minister lives at Number 10 Downing Street, so a new one sees this number on the door.
explanation.definitionFit: The card is one of bridge's five honour cards, and the figure marks the prime minister's official London residence.

clue.text: Resort lacking capital? You bet!.

indicators.note: a capital is a first letter, and lacking it means the opening letter goes

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast

explanation.surface: Asked whether a seaside town lacks money, someone answers emphatically yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks like money; here it is the capital letter at the front of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Right on is an enthusiastic exclamation of agreement, like you bet or absolutely.

clue.text: Stone in the form of ring young lady conceals

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so the first pieces go within the other

parts.note: a girl is a young lady
as means in the capacity of
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A young woman hides a ring-shaped gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A girasol is a fire opal, a gemstone that shows reflections of light, so a precious stone.
